newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in jittery trade, dealers said on Thursday.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S weekly jobless claims, February existing home sales and March University of Michigan consumer sentiment index data, they said.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended March 22 are forecast to be around 313,000 compared with 312,000 reported in the previous week.
Existing home sales for February are expected to rise to 4.05 million against January's 3.94 million.
The University of Michigan consumer index for March is expected to rise to 101.3 percent from 99.7 percent in February.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some position adjustments at the short end," a dealer said.
"All eyes are on tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims, existing home sales and University of Michigan consumer sentiment index figures," he said.
"Most people have squared their positions for the Good Friday holiday weekend, and unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he added.

In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday rose 3/16 percentage point to 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent and weekend rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent. Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
